Tidy Summary of an Evidence Diff

Source: R/evidence_delta.R
evidence_diff_summary.Rd

Rolls an evidence_diff() result up into a small, tidy data.frame: how many rows fell into each change category, how many into each direction, and a single net-movement figure.

Usage

evidence_diff_summary(diff)

Arguments

diff

A data.frame produced by evidence_diff().

Value

A tidy data.frame with one row per metric and two columns, metric (character) and value (numeric). The metrics are n_rows; the change counts n_added, n_removed, n_changed, n_unchanged; the direction counts n_improved, n_regressed, n_neutral; and net_delta. The returned object carries a "net_delta_note" attribute restating that net_delta is a diagnostic, not the SCI.

Details

The net-movement figure, net_delta, is the sum of the signed per-row deltas from evidence_delta() (weighted penalty on the from side minus the to side). A positive net_delta means the submission's weighted penalty load fell overall; a negative one means it rose.

net_delta is a diagnostic rollup only. It is a convenient one-number read on which way a diff moved, not a calibrated readiness score, and it is not the Submission Confidence Index (SCI). Do not report or compare it as an SCI value; use the ecosystem's SCI machinery for that.

See also

evidence_diff() and evidence_delta().

Examples

ctx <- suppressMessages(r4sub_run_context("STUDY1", "DEV"))
mk <- function(id, result, severity) {
  suppressMessages(as_evidence(
    data.frame(
      asset_type = "validation", asset_id = "ADSL",
      source_name = "pinnacle21", indicator_id = id,
      indicator_name = id, indicator_domain = "quality",
      severity = severity, result = result,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ),
    ctx = ctx
  ))
}
old <- suppressMessages(bind_evidence(mk("A", "fail", "high"), mk("B", "pass", "low")))
new <- suppressMessages(bind_evidence(mk("A", "pass", "high"), mk("C", "fail", "medium")))
evidence_diff_summary(evidence_diff(old, new))
#>        metric value
#> 1      n_rows  3.00
#> 2     n_added  1.00
#> 3   n_removed  1.00
#> 4   n_changed  1.00
#> 5 n_unchanged  0.00
#> 6  n_improved  1.00
#> 7 n_regressed  2.00
#> 8   n_neutral  0.00
#> 9   net_delta  0.25
